Measured where a family differs from its backend's design:

* X25519 on libsodium, native: nothing found with arm64's DIT (data-independent timing) bit set, as the lane runs dudect and as Apple requires of constant-time code (link:https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations[Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations]); without it, dudect times `+agree+` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 6.7 to 14.5, against the threshold 10, on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build (2026-11-19): about one nanosecond in 15 µs. libsodium does not set DIT: a program on Apple silicon sets it around its secret operations (link:https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms#Enable-DIT-for-constant-time-cryptographic-operations[Apple, Writing ARM64 code for Apple platforms: enable DIT for constant-time cryptographic operations])
* X25519 on libsodium, wasip2: an open finding, measured and not explained: dudect times `+agree+` with an all-zero secret key against random ones at |t| 13 to 32, against the threshold 10 (a fixed key against another fixed key: 22.9), under wasmtime 47 on an Apple M5 Max, from a release build (2026-11-18), where the native builds pass (|t| 2 to 4); no branch on a secret was found in the WebAssembly or in wasmtime's compiled code, and the cause is unknown. The lane prints this value on wasip2 without judging it; the CI's x86-64 run measures it next
